blocks.text: What's nearby Crescent Beach Ocean Park

Facts here come from the municipality, TransLink or BC Transit, the Ministry of Education and Child Care, and the retailers’ own pages, listed under Sources. Walking and driving times were measured on OpenStreetMap routing on November 2, 2026, from the point named under the table.

items.t: Nearest rapid-transit station: Bridgeport Station (Canada Line), via White Rock Centre on route 351.
Nearest bus exchange: White Rock Centre, served by routes 350, 351, 352 and 361.
Route 350, TransLink: Crescent Beach to White Rock Centre via Crescent Rd, 128 St and 16 Ave.
Route 352, TransLink: Ocean Park to Bridgeport Station via Crescent Rd and 128 St.
Route 361, TransLink: Ocean Park to White Rock Centre via Marine, Russell, Johnston and 152 St.
Crescent Beach, South Surrey: swimming, beach volleyball, beachfront pathway.
Blackie Spit Park, South Surrey: picnic areas, nature trails, two fully fenced dog off-leash spaces.
Crescent Park, South Surrey: 52-hectare park, forest trails, ponds, picnic shelters, tennis and pickleball courts, playground.
Kwomais Point Park, 1367 128 Street, Surrey: ocean lookout over Semiahmoo Bay.
Surrey Libraries Ocean Park Branch, 12854 17 Avenue, Surrey.
Crescent Park Elementary, K-7, SD36, 2440 128 St, Surrey; catchment not confirmed.
Ocean Cliff Elementary, K-7, SD36, 12550 20 Ave, Surrey; catchment not confirmed.
Elgin Park Secondary, 8-12, SD36, 13484 24 Ave, Surrey; catchment not confirmed.

faq.q: Which schools are in and around Crescent Beach and Ocean Park?
faq.a: Schools confirmed by name and address against the BC Ministry K-12 file in this pocket are Crescent Park Elementary (2440 128 St), Ocean Cliff Elementary (12550 20 Ave) and Elgin Park Secondary (13484 24 Ave), with Ray Shepherd Elementary (1650 136 St) also in the pocket — but catchments are address-based, so check the exact address in the SD36 locator before relying on a school (BC Ministry K-12 file, ~/workspace/area-research-2026-11/education/work/bc_k12_schools.csv, read 2026-11-01)

faq.q: Is flooding a consideration in Crescent Beach?
faq.a: It is worth checking for the specific property: the live page, citing the City of Surrey, describes Crescent Beach as low-lying at the mouth of the Nicomekl River, notes the City's 2019 Coastal Flood Adaptation Strategy, and reports about 70% of properties now have a storm sewer fronting or flanking them after the utility improvements — ask about the property and check insurance before removing subjects

faq.q: Where can I walk to the beach in Crescent Beach?
faq.a: The live page, citing the City of Surrey, lists Beecher Street, Sullivan Street and Target Street as the best Crescent Beach access points, and Blackie Spit Park at 3136 McBride Avenue reaches into Mud Bay at the mouth of the Nicomekl River
